senses.sense_definition: To inflict severe physical damage on a person or animal, especially by cutting off or destroying a limb or essential part.

examples.text: The cruel trap was designed to severely <w>mutilate</w> any animal caught inside it.
Exploding artillery shells can kill or permanently <w>mutilate</w> soldiers on the front line.

senses.sense_definition: To destroy, deface, or ruin something so severely that it is rendered unrecognizable or unusable.

examples.text: The vandals chose to intentionally <w>mutilate</w> currency by shredding the paper bills.
Protesters began to <w>mutilate</w> the historic statue until its facial features were ruined.

senses.sense_definition: To damage or spoil the integrity, meaning, or quality of something by cutting or altering parts of it.

examples.text: The government censors proceeded to heavily <w>mutilate</w> the script before permitting its performance.
She worried that heavy editing would <w>mutilate</w> the original message of her novel.

senses.sense_definition: An individual, animal, or object that has suffered mutilation.

examples.text: The old war clinic provided special prosthetics for each surviving <w>mutilate</w>.
Among the recovered artifacts was a damaged <w>mutilate</w> that could no longer be identified.

senses.sense_definition: Deprived of or missing an important limb, organ, or structural part; mutilated.

examples.text: The archaeologist unearthed a <w>mutilate</w> statue that was missing its head and arms.
Old medical records described the patient as having a <w>mutilate</w> hand after the accident.

senses.sense_definition: Having flukes or fin-like limbs instead of rear legs, as in cetaceans.

examples.text: Early naturalists classified the dolphin as a <w>mutilate</w> mammal adapted completely to aquatic life.
Whales display a <w>mutilate</w> body plan characterized by tail flukes rather than hind legs.
